featureName: Apply every typed identity mutation to its committed specification vectors

scenarios.name: Apply <id> to its committed before-snapshot fixture [id=sign-in, account=grace, wasAccount=ada]

steps.text: the committed before-snapshot, mutation and outcome fixtures for the sign-in kind
the resulting record matches the committed after-snapshot, holds the grace session, no longer holds ada, and reports the committed outcome

scenarios.name: Apply <id> to its committed before-snapshot fixture [id=sign-out, account=none, wasAccount=ada]

steps.text: the committed before-snapshot, mutation and outcome fixtures for the sign-out kind
the resulting record matches the committed after-snapshot, holds the none session, no longer holds ada, and reports the committed outcome

scenarios.name: Undoing <id> restores the committed before-snapshot fixture [id=sign-in, account=grace, wasAccount=ada]

steps.text: the committed before-snapshot and mutation fixtures for the sign-in kind
sign-in is applied and then its own computed inverse steps are applied
the record equals the committed before-snapshot again and holds the ada session with its original token and issue time

scenarios.name: Undoing <id> restores the committed before-snapshot fixture [id=sign-out, account=none, wasAccount=ada]

steps.text: the committed before-snapshot and mutation fixtures for the sign-out kind
sign-out is applied and then its own computed inverse steps are applied
the record equals the committed before-snapshot again and holds the ada session with its original token and issue time

scenarios.name: Signing out of a record that already holds no session has no undo step to offer

steps.text: the committed after-snapshot of the sign-out vector, which holds no session
sign-out is applied to it and its own inverse steps are computed from that same record
the record stays signed out and the inverse is empty rather than a sign-in carrying a fabricated session

scenarios.name: Decode and re-encode the committed signed-in record without passing bytes through

steps.text: the committed before-snapshot of the sign-in vector
the record is decoded into IdentitySetting and re-encoded from the typed value alone
the re-encoded projection is the committed one, field for field, and the decode is proven real by reading the account and its token back off the typed value rather than off the text
